hints: Look for the one step that needs ATP. Pumping protons out of the companion cell must come before protons can flow back in, so ask which event has to be first.

Remember the cause and effect chain for loading: proton gradient drives sucrose into the companion cell, then sucrose into the sieve tube, which lowers water potential, so water follows by osmosis and builds up hydrostatic pressure last.
walkthrough:
**Start with active transport**

Think of loading like charging a battery first. Companion cells use ATP to pump protons (H+) out (5). This creates a steep proton gradient with many H+ outside.

This has to be the starter, nothing else can happen without this energy input.

**Co-transport sucrose into the companion cell, then to the sieve tube**

Protons now want to flow back in down their gradient. They do this through a co-transporter that drags sucrose with them into the companion cell (2). Sucrose then moves on through plasmodesmata into the sieve tube element (1).

**Lower water potential, then water enters by osmosis**

More sucrose in the sieve tube means more solute, so its water potential decreases (4). Water from the nearby xylem now moves down its water potential gradient into the sieve tube by osmosis (6).

**Build hydrostatic pressure for mass flow**

That extra water increases the volume and turgor inside the tube. This produces a very high hydrostatic pressure at the source (3), which pushes the sap along for mass flow. So the order is 5 to 2 to 1 to 4 to 6 to 3.

options.A: Starts with sucrose already in the sieve tube (1) and puts active pumping (5) in the middle, which is backwards because the proton gradient must be created before co-transport can work.
options.B: Starts with high hydrostatic pressure (3) and ends with decreased water potential (4), but pressure is the final result of water entry, not the starting cause.
options.C: Puts pressure (3) first and water movement (6) last, which reverses cause and effect because water entry by osmosis must happen before pressure can build up.
options.D: Correct logical chain: pump H+ out (5), co-transport H+ and sucrose in (2), sucrose to sieve tube (1), water potential falls (4), water enters by osmosis (6), hydrostatic pressure builds (3).
